To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

semantic information can be used to guide geometric representation for self supervised monoocular depth estimation, and that a two stage training can be used to overcome a semantic bias on dynamic object.

(1) semantic information can be used to improve the self supervised representation learning for depth prediction, (2) the semantic bias on dynamic object can be overcome by resampling and (3) the proposed method improves the state of the arts in all metrics for self supervised monocalar depth prediction

1) we show that semantic information can be leveraged in self-supervised monocular depth learning to guide the representation learning process; 2) we propose an architecture that uses semantic information to guide the representation; 3) we show that our method outperforms the state of the arts in terms of overall performance, details and per category; 4) we propose a two-stage training process that overcomes a common semantic bias in dynamic objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we leverage category level semantic information for self supervised representation learning for depth prediction?
the question how to leverage semantic structure for self supervised representation learning for monocular depth prediction.
two main questions: (1) how to leverage semantic information to improve self supervised representation learning for depth estimation and (2) how to address the semantic bias on dynamic object.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we show that self supervised monocular learning is indeed capable of learning geometric representations that relate appearance to 3d properties.
our method is the state of the-art on self-supervised monocular depth estimation.
our method is able to learn more semantic aware representations, which are able to capture more accurate geometric structure, and are more robust to semantic bias on dynamic object.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semantic information is crucial for self-supervised depth estimation, and our approach shows the best results in this direction.
semantic segmentation can be used to guide geometric representation in a self supervised manner to improve the performance of a depth prediction network.
we propose a new way to leverage semantic segmentation for self supervised representation learning for monocular depth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semantic priors can be used to guide geometric representation in a self supervised manner, and that the resulting representation can then be used for a wide range of vision tasks.
semantic information is an important cue to guide geometric self supervised representation learning, and should not be neglected.
semantic priors can be used in a self supervised fashion, without requiring any additional labels or proxy losses.
